title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend: ask what's new, tell them about your weekend and the big news since you last met, ask 'have you ever…?', say what you were doing when something happened, and use 'ago', 'since' and 'for'.
intro:
You bump into an old friend in the bazaar: **ڪهڙو اتفاق آهي!** Within a minute you'll be asked **حال احوال ٻڌاءِ!** 'tell me all your news' — who got married, who moved, who's started going to the gym. This unit is about telling and asking for that news.

The grammar is about time: the difference between **ويس** 'I went' and **ويو آهيان** 'I have been', **پيو ڪندو هوس** 'I was doing', and the little words for time spans: ٽي سال **اڳ** 'three years ago', عيد **کان وٺي** 'since Eid', ٻن مهينن **کان** 'for two months (and still)'.

grammar.title: 'I went' or 'I have been'? Past and present perfect
grammar.body:
Sindhi has the same two choices as English, built from the past participle (Unit 16):

**Simple past** — finished time: مان ڪالهه ڪراچي **ويس** 'I went to Karachi yesterday'.
**Present perfect** — participle + present of 'to be' (آهيان، آهين، آهي، آهيون، آهيو، آهن): مان ڪراچي **ويو آهيان** 'I have been to Karachi'.

**When to use the perfect:**
• **news and results that matter now**: هن کي پٽ **ٿيو آهي** 'she's had a baby boy', تون **بدلجي ويو آهين** 'you've changed'
• **experience — 'have you ever…?'**: **ڪڏهن** + perfect: توهان ڪڏهن ٿر **ويا آهيو**؟
• **'never'** = ڪڏهن **به نه**; **'not yet'** = **اڃا ڪونه / اڃا نه**

**When to use the simple past:** with any finished time word — ڪالهه، گذريل هفتي، ويڪ اينڊ تي، ٽي سال اڳ: ويڪ اينڊ تي ڇا **ڪيو**؟ (not ڇا ڪيو آهي).

**Agreement doesn't change.** Intransitive verbs agree with the subject (مان ويو آهيان / مان وئي آهيان), and transitive verbs are **ergative** in the perfect too — oblique doer, verb agreeing with the object: مون نئين نوڪري **شروع ڪئي آهي** (نوڪري f), مون پلو مڇي **چکي آهي** (مڇي f), مون سمنڊ **ڏٺو آهي** (m).

**Had done** (past perfect) uses the past of 'to be': اسين **مليا هئاسين** 'we had met', مون **ٻڌو هو** 'I had heard'. In casual speech you'll also hear the perfect with personal endings — **ڏٺو اٿم** 'I've seen it', **ڪيو اٿئي؟** 'have you done it?' — recognise them; the full forms are always correct.

grammar.title: 'I was doing': the past continuous
grammar.body:
To say what was going on at a moment in the past — often when something else happened — Sindhi has two forms.

**1. The Sindhi form: پيو + -ndo + past of 'to be'.** All three parts agree with the subject (پيو / پئي / پيا / پيون):
مان ڪم **پيو ڪندو هوس** — I was working (m)
مان ڪم **پئي ڪندي هيس** — I was working (f)
هو **پيو ايندو هو** — he was coming
هوءَ **پئي ايندي هئي** — she was coming
اسين **پيا کائيندا هئاسين** — we were eating
مينهن **پيو وسندو هو** — it was raining

**2. The Urdu-style form: stem in -ī / -e + رهيو + past of 'to be'** — easier to build, also very common, especially in cities: مان سمهي **رهيو هوس** 'I was sleeping', ٻار کيڏي **رهيا هئا** 'the kids were playing'.

Neither form is ergative: the subject stays as it is (**مان** ماني پيو کائيندو هوس, not مون).

The typical sentence links it to an event with **جڏهن … تڏهن / ته**: **جڏهن** تنهنجو فون آيو، مان **پيو سمهندو هوس** 'when your call came, I was sleeping'.

Compare with 'used to' (Unit 26): **ڪندو هوس** without پيو = I used to do; **پيو ڪندو هوس** = I was doing (at that moment).

examples.en: When your call came, I was asleep. (man)

grammar.title: Ago, since and for: اڳ، کان وٺي، کان
grammar.body:
**Ago** — time + **اڳ** aɠu: ٽي سال **اڳ** 'three years ago', ٻه ڏينهن **اڳ** 'two days ago', ٿورو **اڳ** 'a little while ago'. Used with the simple past.

**Since** — oblique + **کان وٺي** khāṃ vaṭhī: عيد **کان وٺي** 'since Eid', ٻارهين ڪلاس **کان وٺي** 'since twelfth grade'. Since an event = **جڏهن کان** + clause: **جڏهن کان** هو لڏي ويو آهي 'since he moved away'.

**For** depends on whether it's still going on:
• **finished**: just the time, no postposition (or **تائين**): مان **ٻه سال** لاهور ۾ رهيس 'I lived in Lahore for two years'.
• **still going on** ('have been … for'): the **present** + time in the oblique + **کان**: اسين **ٽن سالن کان** هتي **رهون ٿا** 'we've been living here for three years'. English uses a perfect here; Sindhi uses the present — a classic mistake for learners. (Unit 32 uses this a lot for symptoms.)

**How long?** = **ڪڏهن کان**…؟ 'since when?' (still going on) or **ڪيترو عرصو**…؟ 'for how long?'.

Remember the oblique before کان: ٻه سال → **ٻن سالن** کان، ٽي مهينا → **ٽن مهينن** کان، هڪ هفتو → **هڪ هفتي** کان.

dialogue.title: Old friends at the chai stall
dialogue.setting: Sunday morning outside a chai stall near Rani Bagh, Hyderabad. Zubair and Bilawal were at school together and haven't seen each other for years. They talk like old friends — تون، يار.

lines.en: And what about you? I heard you'd gone abroad.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: ها، ٽي سال دبئي ۾ نوڪري ڪئي. گذريل هفتي ئي واپسي ٿي آهي.

lines.native: واهه! پوءِ هل، چانهه پيئون — پنجن سالن جو حال احوال ٻڌڻو آهي!
lines.roman: vāh! poi halu, chānhi pīūṃ — panjan sālan jo hāl ahvāl ɓudhaṇo āhe!

lines.roman: halu! para chānhi tunhinjī tarafāṃ — dhīu jī miṭhāī bi khārāiṇī pavandī!
lines.en: Let's go! But the tea's on you — and you owe me sweets for the baby!

culture:
**Catching up is a ritual.** A Sindhi greeting between friends who haven't met for a while is never just 'hi': expect a hug, **ڪهڙو اتفاق!** or **ڪٿي گم هئين؟** 'where did you disappear to?', and then a long round of questions about family — **گهر ۾ سڀ خير؟** 'everyone well at home?', parents' health, children, marriage, work. Asking a man in his late twenties **شادي ٿي؟** 'got married yet?' is completely normal; so is asking how much a new job pays, though younger people are starting to find that nosy.

**Good news means sweets.** A new baby, a wedding, a new job, passing exams, coming back from abroad — the person with the news is expected to give **مٺائي** ('sweets are owed': مٺائي کارائڻي پوندي!). Coming back from **عمرو** or Hajj, people bring dates and Zamzam water for friends and neighbours.

Weekends are mostly Saturday evening and Sunday: family visits, a **پڪنڪ** at Keenjhar Lake or the beaches at Hawke's Bay and Sea View in Karachi, a drive to Rani Bagh in Hyderabad, or simply a long lunch. Monsoon is the season for **پلو** fish — friends will ask whether you've tried it yet, and won't accept 'not yet' as an answer for long.

tip.title: What's new: the present perfect
tip.body:
- Participle + **آهي** (آهيان، آهين، آهيون…) = has / have done: هو **آيو آهي**، تون **بدلجي ويو آهين**.
- Transitive verbs stay ergative and agree with the object: مون نوڪري **شروع ڪئي آهي**.
- Use it for news that matters now.

lessons.title: How was your weekend?

tip.title: Finished time → simple past
tip.body:
- With ڪالهه، گذريل هفتي، ويڪ اينڊ تي… use the **simple past**: ويڪ اينڊ تي ڇا **ڪيو**؟
- The perfect is for news with no finished time: مان ٿڪجي **ويو آهيان** 'I'm worn out'.
- Same agreement: مون فلمون **ڏٺيون**، اسين پڪنڪ تي **وياسين**.

tip.title: Ever, never, not yet
tip.body:
- 'Have you ever…?' = **ڪڏهن** + perfect: توهان **ڪڏهن** ٿر **ويا آهيو**؟
- 'Never' = **ڪڏهن به نه**: مون **ڪڏهن به** پلو مڇي **نه** چکي آهي.
- 'Not yet' = **اڃا ڪونه / اڃا نه**. 'The first time' = **پهريون ڀيرو**.

sentences.roman: hā, ɓa sāla aɠu amāṃ sāṃ ʿumro kayum.
sentences.en: Yes, I did Umrah with Mum two years ago.

sentences.native: جهاز ۾ اهو منهنجو پهريون ڀيرو هو.
sentences.roman: jahāza meṃ uho munhinjo pahiryoṃ bhero ho.
sentences.en: That was my first time on a plane.

sentences.native: اسين ڪڏهن به موهن جو دڙو نه ويا آهيون.
sentences.roman: asīṃ kaɗahiṃ bi mohan jo daṛo na vayā āhyūṃ.
sentences.en: We've never been to Mohenjo-daro.

sentences.native: هوءَ اڃا ڪونه آئي آهي.
sentences.roman: hūa añā kona āī āhe.
sentences.en: She hasn't come yet.

sentences.native: هي سنڌي ماني چکي ڏس!
sentences.roman: hī sindhī mānī chakhī ɗisu!
sentences.en: Have a taste of this Sindhi food! (informal)

sentences.native: تو ڪڏهن سمنڊ ڏٺو آهي؟
sentences.roman: to kaɗahiṃ samunḍu ɗiṭho āhe?
sentences.en: Have you ever seen the sea? (informal)

tip.title: Was doing: پيو + -ndo + هو
tip.body:
- **پيو** + -ndo form + past of 'be', all agreeing: مان ڪم **پيو ڪندو هوس** (m), **پئي ڪندي هيس** (f).
- Easier city form: **-ي رهيو هوس**: ٻار کيڏي **رهيا هئا**.
- No ergative: **مان** ماني پيو کائيندو هوس.
- Without پيو it means 'used to'.
tip.pattern: پيو / پئي / پيا + verb-ndo + هو / هئي / هئا

sentences.native: ڪالهه هن وقت مان ڪم پيو ڪندو هوس.
sentences.roman: kālha hin vaqta māṃ kamu peyo kando hos.
sentences.en: This time yesterday I was working. (man)

sentences.native: اسين توهان کي ئي ياد پيا ڪندا هئاسين!
sentences.roman: asīṃ tavhāṃ khe ī yāda pyā kandā huāsīṃ!
sentences.en: We were just thinking about you!

sentences.native: هوءَ ڪورس پئي ڪندي هئي، تنهن ڪري ملي نه سگهي.
sentences.roman: hūa kōrsu paī kandī huī, tanhin kare milī na saghī.
sentences.en: She was doing a course, so she couldn't meet.

sentences.native: وچ ۾ ڪجهه مهينا مان لاهور ۾ پيو رهندو هوس.
sentences.roman: vicha meṃ kujhu mahīnā māṃ lāhora meṃ peyo rahando hos.
sentences.en: For a few months in between I was living in Lahore. (man)

sentences.native: مينهن پيو وسندو هو، تنهن ڪري اسين گهر ۾ رهياسين.
sentences.roman: mīṃhu peyo vasando ho, tanhin kare asīṃ ghara meṃ rahyāsīṃ.
sentences.en: It was raining, so we stayed at home.

sentences.native: ٻار گهٽيءَ ۾ کيڏي رهيا هئا.
sentences.roman: ɓāra ghiṭīa meṃ kheɗī rahyā huā.
sentences.en: The kids were playing in the street.

sentences.native: مون توکي ڏاڍو ياد ڪيو.
sentences.roman: moṃ tokhe ɗāḍho yāda kayo.
sentences.en: I missed you a lot.

sentences.native: وچ ۾ مان ٻه ڀيرا ڪراچي ويس.
sentences.roman: vicha meṃ māṃ ɓa bherā karāchī viyus.
sentences.en: In between I went to Karachi twice. (man)

sentences.native: تون ڪهڙو ڪورس پيو ڪرين؟
sentences.roman: tūṃ kahiṛo kōrsu peyo kareṃ?
sentences.en: Which course are you doing? (informal)

tip.title: اڳ · کان وٺي · for
tip.body:
- **ago** = time + **اڳ**: ٽي سال **اڳ**.
- **since** = **کان وٺي**: عيد **کان وٺي**; since an event = **جڏهن کان** …
- **for** (finished): just the time: ٻه سال لاهور ۾ **رهيس**.
- The time goes oblique before کان: ٻه سال → **ٻن سالن** کان.

sentences.native: هنن ٻه سال اڳ نئون گهر ورتو.
sentences.roman: hunan ɓa sāla aɠu naoṃ gharu varto.
sentences.en: They bought a new house two years ago.

sentences.native: هو جمعي کان وٺي بيمار آهي.
sentences.roman: hū jumʿe khāṃ vaṭhī bīmāru āhe.
sentences.en: He's been ill since Friday.

sentences.native: توهان جي واپسي ڪڏهن ٿي؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ jī vāpasī kaɗahiṃ thī?
sentences.en: When did you get back?

sentences.native: مان ٽي مهينا دبئي ۾ رهيس.
sentences.roman: māṃ ṭe mahīnā dubaī meṃ rahyus.
sentences.en: I stayed in Dubai for three months. (man)

sentences.native: ٽي مهينا ڪيئن گذري ويا، خبر ئي نه پئي.
sentences.roman: ṭe mahīnā kīeṃ guzrī vayā, xabara ī na paī.
sentences.en: Three months flew by — I didn't even notice.

sentences.native: اهو تازو ئي ٿيو آهي.
sentences.roman: uho tāzo ī thiyo āhe.
sentences.en: That's only just happened.

sentences.native: جڏهن کان هو لڏي ويو آهي، فون ئي نٿو ڪري.
sentences.roman: jaɗahiṃ khāṃ hū laḍī vayo āhe, fon ī natho kare.
sentences.en: Since he moved away, he doesn't even call.

sentences.native: اسين ڪيترا سال اڳ مليا هئاسين؟
sentences.roman: asīṃ ketirā sāla aɠu milyā huāsīṃ?
sentences.en: How many years ago did we meet?

sentences.native: منهنجا گهرڀاتي حيدرآباد لڏي آيا آهن.
sentences.roman: munhinjā gharbhātī haidarābād laḍī āyā āhin.
sentences.en: My family have moved to Hyderabad.

lessons.title: New habits

tip.title: 'Have been doing for' = present + کان
tip.body:
- Still going on? Use the **present** + oblique time + **کان**: ٻن مهينن **کان** جم **وڃان ٿو** 'I've been going to the gym for two months'.
- Ask **ڪڏهن کان**…؟ 'how long…?'
- Finished? Past, no postposition: ٻه مهينا جم **ويس**.

new: مون جم وڃڻ شروع ڪيو آهي.

sentences.native: مان ٻن مهينن کان جم وڃان ٿو.
sentences.roman: māṃ ɓin mahīnan khāṃ jima vañāṃ tho.
sentences.en: I've been going to the gym for two months. (man)

sentences.native: ڪڏهن کان ڊائٽ تي آهين؟
sentences.roman: kaɗahiṃ khāṃ ḍāiṭa te āhīṃ?
sentences.en: How long have you been dieting? (informal)

sentences.native: منهنجو وزن پنج ڪلو گهٽ ٿيو آهي.
sentences.roman: munhinjo vaznu panja kilo ghaṭu thiyo āhe.
sentences.en: I've lost five kilos.

sentences.native: هوءَ عيد کان وٺي مٺو نٿي کائي.
sentences.roman: hūa ʿīda khāṃ vaṭhī miṭho nathī khāe.
sentences.en: She hasn't had anything sweet since Eid.

sentences.native: ڊائٽ ٻه ڏينهن هلي، پوءِ برياني آئي!
sentences.roman: ḍāiṭa ɓa ɗīṃha halī, poi biryānī āī!
sentences.en: The diet lasted two days — then the biryani arrived!

sentences.native: اسين هڪ هفتي کان هتي رهون ٿا.
sentences.roman: asīṃ hika hafte khāṃ hite rahūṃ thā.
sentences.en: We've been staying here for a week.

sentences.native: جم کان پوءِ مان ڏاڍو ٿڪجي پوان ٿو.
sentences.roman: jima khāṃ poi māṃ ɗāḍho thakjī pavāṃ tho.
sentences.en: After the gym I get really tired. (man)

sentences.native: تون ته ڏاڍو سمارٽ ٿي ويو آهين! ڪڏهن کان جم ٿو وڃين؟
sentences.roman: tūṃ ta ɗāḍho smārṭu thī vayo āhīṃ! kaɗahiṃ khāṃ jima tho vañeṃ?
sentences.en: You've got really slim! How long have you been going to the gym?

sentences.native: مون ڪالهه کان ڊائٽ شروع ڪئي آهي.
sentences.roman: moṃ kālha khāṃ ḍāiṭa shurūʿ kaī āhe.
sentences.en: I started a diet yesterday.
